response.title: Is a portable power station or a dedicated CPAP battery the better buy for home power outages?
response.answer:
For home power outages, a portable power station is usually the better buy than a dedicated CPAP battery. It generally offers more battery capacity per dollar, can power other household essentials, and is easier to recharge during extended outages.

However, a dedicated CPAP battery can be the better choice if your top priority is keeping your CPAP running reliably through the night, particularly if you want a compact backup that automatically takes over when the power fails.

The biggest distinction is that battery capacity and power delivery matter more than the product's label. A 500 Wh portable power station can provide substantially more runtime than a 100 Wh dedicated CPAP battery, assuming both can efficiently power your machine.

How much battery capacity do you actually need?

+1

Power stations worth considering

BLUETTI AC50P Portable Power Station – 504Wh LiFePO4, 700W

504 Wh · LiFePO4 · 700W output

$339.00

A reasonable capacity for one night with heating enabled or multiple nights without, depending on actual consumption.

BLUETTI AC180 Solar Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,152Wh

1,152 Wh · 1,800W output

$499.00

Better suited to extended outages and charging phones or other small electronics alongside the CPAP.

What I would prioritize

For home use, I would look for a 500–1,000 Wh LiFePO4 power station with pure sine wave AC output, a compatible DC output, and verified automatic switchover if uninterrupted operation is important.

One important caveat: a power station advertised as having UPS functionality is not automatically suitable as an uninterrupted medical-device backup. Test whether your CPAP continues operating during a simulated outage, and confirm compatibility with the manufacturer. Using an approved DC converter can also improve efficiency. 
Runtime, Humidifier and DC Power
+1

One question that could change my recommendation: Which CPAP machine do you have—ResMed AirSense 10, AirSense 11, Philips DreamStation, or another model?

With that information, I can recommend the appropriate battery size and help determine whether a dedicated CPAP battery would actually be worth the extra cost.
